BiblicalUsage: Ratsa' means to pierce — to bore through with an awl. The law says of the servant who loves his master and will not go out free, 'then his master shall bring him unto the judges... and his master shall bore his ear through with an aul; and he shall serve him for ever.'
TheologicalSignificance: I hear this saying that the pierced ear is love's mark: the servant chose to stay, and the awl wrote his choice on his ear for all to see.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
